correctness.rationale: At stationarity \((A,R)=(UL,(1-U)L)\) with \(U\) uniform and independent of the size-biased interval length \(L\). Expanding moments gives the displayed covariance decomposition into a nonnegative term \(B(r+1,s+1)\operatorname{Cov}(L^r,L^s)\) plus the fixed negative split term, and the analogous variance decompositions. Monotonicity of both powers of \(L\) gives nonnegative covariance, proving the lower bound; equality forces both transformed variances of \(L\) to vanish and hence deterministic \(L\). For a positive covariance, discarding the negative mean term and using Cauchy--Schwarz gives the strict upper constant. A two-point \(L\) makes \(L^r,L^s\) perfectly correlated; choosing its rare large atom makes squared means negligible relative to variances, reaching the upper endpoint in the limit. Size-bias inversion produces a valid two-point interarrival law, and continuity fills the interval.

value.rationale: Age and residual life are canonical renewal variables, and the equal-power range was already singled out as a natural solved case. Completing the unequal-power problem with exact endpoints, equality/nonattainment behavior and full interval realization is a natural structural extension with reusable dependence bounds.

final_claim: For a stationary renewal process with positive interarrival time and finite moments as stated, the Pearson correlation \(\operatorname{Corr}(A^r,R^s)\) for unequal positive powers \(r\ne s\) has the exact distribution-free range \([\ell_{r,s},u_{r,s})\) displayed in RESULT.md; deterministic interarrivals uniquely attain the lower endpoint, two-point interarrival laws attain every interior value and approach the upper endpoint, and exponential interarrivals give correlation zero.
limitations: Stationary renewal age/residual life and Pearson correlation only.
The upper endpoint is a supremum, not an attained maximum.
The required moment assumptions are those ensuring both transformed variances are finite.
